body: Update: This seems especially present with chunked file uploads.
Sorry for spamming this issue, but is it related to #222?

Hmm, chunked files.

Can you paste a log with `-vv` of uploading a chunked file that you think might have a problem?

Are there retries involved?

Can you check with the latest beta that this is still a problem?

@ncw Sure, please allow me a few days to experiment a little.

There are no retries. While I haven't investigated specifically, it appears to be reading the file or encrypting it at the bandwidth limit and then uploading each chunk at full throttle. There are lulls between preparing chunks.

Your explanation sounds correct looking at the code.

Which means on average the transfer rate will be what you set, however it will burst to very high while it is sending the chunks.

I agree this isn't ideal especially since B2 chunks are 100MB.

I could put the bandwidth limit on the other side of the buffer, but then that will have the opposite problem if you are copying from a network remote to B2.

Having a bandwidth limiter on both sides of the buffer would work, but that will limit the bandwidth too much since both limiters will be taking from the same pool.

Perhaps two limiters at twice the bandwidth...

I'm sure there is a simple solution, it just hasn't come to me yet!
It sounds like this would be a good argument for two pools - perhaps --read-bw-limit and --write-bw-limit? --src-bw-limit and --dest-bw-limit?

Also, at least in my case I'm reading from a local filesystem. Would it make sense to move the bandwidth limiter on the opposite side of the buffer when the source is a local filesystem and the destination a remote? I can see that at least being a short term solution.

Two pools is the conclusion I came to as well. I'd set them both to bwlimit. I like your idea of bypassing them for local  disk read or write.

I'll have a play with some of those ideas.

As you can see below, for a few minutes the number of checks and the number of transfers does not increase.

.
Fortunately after a while (sometimes a few minutes, sometimes many), things resume. So this is not a fatal issue.

**I am guessing that b2 is throttling. If that is the case, is there anything I can do to prevent it?**

I am using rclone v 1.35 with `--checkers 8 --transfers 8 --bwlimit 700k --filter-from large-filter-file`

I don't think it is the case that rclone is simply chugging through filtered-out files during this time, because I see no disk activity in my OS monitor (gkrellm).

body: Awesome! Thank you for looking into this - I really appreciate it.

Experiencing similar behavior with Google Drive. With the limiter, the average speed is set to the limiter, but I suppose each chunk runs full speed and then waits again. This causes occasional stutters in streams I'm watching.  Turning off the bandwidth limiter in general doesn't affect the max speed, just removes those pauses. On 1.36 and I experience this on Windows 10 Pro x64 and Windows Server 2016 if that matters.

![2017-05-30 17_16_52-2017-05-30 11_41_24-task manager png - photos](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/29075734/26606490/1ca426a8-4560-11e7-870c-99005d81fe02.png)

No errors when viewing with -vv, simply mentioning when chunks were sent.

Edit: To be completely clear, the average speed is the same as what the bwlimiter is set to, but the spikes in bandwidth are the issue. So the limit is working, just not as expected.
@SirCrest this is likely the same issue... I'll update the title of this issue accordingly!

rename.to: --bwlimit ignored for chunked uploads on b2 & drive (& others?)

body:
I noticed that with drive the `--bwlimit` does not work well with slow uplinks (eg. 5 MBps) unless you also lower the chunk size. For example on a 5 MBps link I used a chunk size of 256 KB instead of the default 8 MB. After lowering the chunk size, rclone was staying very close to the 350 KByte/s bwlimit I had set, while it undershot a lot with the default chunk size.

I haven't had to use bwlimit since upgrading my upstream to 40 MBps and using QoS on my router, so I don't know if the above observation still applies to current rclone versions (I think it must have been on v1.32-v1.34).
@felixbuenemann This is potentially very helpful. Thanks!

I'm also seeing some weird behavior with --bwlimit and --chunk-size and i'm unsure if this is normal or not. I have a limit of 2 transfer set on box and when it's uploading with 2 items at a chunk limit of 8M, it works fine, saturates all the way up to my --bwlimit of 2.3M. However when i have only 1 item transfer at a chunk size of just 8M it seems to struggle to get a transfer speed of 1.2M. If i try increasing the chunk size, up to 128M or 256M, it seems to work peaks above my --bwlimit sometimes, but once it appears to upload that chunk, the speeds drop to basically 64K for 2 to 3 minutes then they pick back up to the --bwlimit, then once that chunk is done uploading rinse and repeat as described aboved. I'm unsure if that's a consequence of using --chunk flag but i didn't see this issue when i used a vps with large chunk sizes without the --bwlimit flag.

I am pretty sure the issue for Google Drive will be fixed with #970, #968. You can try the beta here:
https://www.breunig.xyz/share/rclone-beta/v1.36-232-gb2b5c629-drive-accounting%CE%B2/
